races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Adeel
runners_data.spotlight: £42,500 yearling, £70,000 breeze-up 2yo; third foal; by Havana Grey; brother to 6f winner Tawasol (RPR 97); dam 6f winner (including 2yo/AW; 78), half-sister to 6f Group 3 winner Tabdeed; yard among the winners recently but this looks a hot contest in which to make his debut.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.spotlight: 55,000euros yearling, £115,000 breeze-up 2yo; third foal; by Sioux Nation; closely related to 5f/6f AW winner Midnight Call (RPR 69); dam once-raced close relative of 6f 2yo Listed winner Cape Factor, half-sister to winners My Eyes Adore You (6f Listed) and Court House (smart 1m-1m4f); has a speedy pedigree and worth a market check; wears hood for debut.

runners_data.name: Rapid Deployment
runners_data.spotlight: 42,000gns yearling; first foal; by Zoustar; dam multiple 5f AW winner (including 2yo; RPR 104), half-sister to winners No Jet Lag (US 1m Grade 2) and Optari (French Group-placed 6f 2yo), out of 6f 2yo Listed winner; yard going well and 3-8 with their juveniles this year; likely contender on this debut.

runners_data.name: Rattenbury
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000euros foal, 75,000euros yearling; fifth foal; Blackbeard half-brother to 6f AW winner Dyed In The Wool (RPR 74); dam 5f 2yo winner (76), half-sister to four winners out of US 6f stakes winner; not ruled out on debut but he may well improve for the outing.

runners_data.name: Storm Blade
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth foal; by Night Of Thunder; brother to 6f/1m AW winner Storm Star (RPR 106), half-brother to 6f 2yo winner Planet Seeker (80); dam 6f/7f winner (including 2yo/Group 3; 113), half-sister to winners Foxtrot Lady (7f Group 3) and Dance Of Fire (useful 1m-1m2f including 2yo); yard going well and no surprise were he to feature on this debut.

runners_data.name: Bulletsnap
runners_data.spotlight: 85,000euros foal; second foal; by Minzaal; dam French Listed-placed 7.5f-8.5f winner (including 2yo/AW; RPR 93), sister to useful French 1m-1m4f winner Anobe, out of French 10.5f winning half-sister to prolific 7f-8.5f winner Vert Et Blanc; stable's second juvenile runner of the season; trainer  in great form so must be considered on debut.

runners_data.name: Mrair
runners_data.spotlight: Turned over at short odds on debut when runner-up at Newmarket (6f, good) 17 days ago where the Dip looked to put him out; nevertheless he still caught the eye and may warrant another chance with Ryan Moore on board.

runners_data.name: Rogue Imperial
runners_data.spotlight: Caught the eye on debut when fifth of eight at Yarmouth (6f, good; 3-1) 12 days ago when, after travelling well, he looked to blow up; should benefit from the run and ought to go well.

runners_data.name: Blue Skies Above
runners_data.spotlight: Beat only one home on his debut at Kempton (6f, AW; 11-2) last month; makes turf debut and needs to have come on leaps and bounds.

races.name: Follow @AtTheRaces On Instagram Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Perola
runners_data.note: Only front runner likely to get uncontested lead but coming back from 91-day layoff after wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on three of his four runs, last time finishing third over 7f at Wolverhampton; has since had wind surgery; interesting, but was below par only previous run on turf.

runners_data.name: Star Banner
runners_data.note: Lightly raced improver from good connections who should handle step up in class with recent experience
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal of a 6f juvenile winner; shaped with promise when third in a Musselburgh novice 11 days ago (7f, good); bit green that day so should fare even better this time.

runners_data.name: Kennington
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse proven at this course and distance with Probert's 18% strike rate for Morrison
runners_data.spotlight: Creditable third in a 1m maiden on the AW here in April; should improve on that and worth considering.

runners_data.name: Chasse Patate
runners_data.note: Promising debut third who carries 7lb claimer and represents in-form Watson stable
runners_data.spotlight: Made late headway to take third in a Kempton novice on debut 12 days ago (7f; 28-1, Santiago Boy back in fifth); should improve; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Mythological Star
runners_data.note: Weak maiden form suggests outclassed despite likely improvement from debut effort
runners_data.spotlight: 19,000euros yearling; didn't show a great deal on last month's Kempton debut (66-1) but is a likely improver.

runners_data.name: Santiago Boy
runners_data.note: Finished behind Chasse Patate last time and faces same rival off identical weights
runners_data.spotlight: Improved on his debut run when 3l fifth in a Kempton novice last time (7f, standard to slow; 125-1, bit to find with third-placed Chasse Patate); further progress likely; each-way chance.

runners_data.name: The Bureau Club
runners_data.note: Slow starter who needs strong pace to be effective but zero wins from six starts for Pike
runners_data.spotlight: Habitual slow starter whose best effort by some way was when fourth in a Kempton maiden in March (1m); lesser efforts either side of that, including on turf debut at Salisbury last time (7f, good to firm; beaten 11.5l); bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Ocean Force
runners_data.note: Veteran with poor form who appears outclassed in this company despite course experience
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten all starts so far, last time finishing 16l fifth of nine in a C&D novice; hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Perola will take them along as the only confirmed front runner, setting what should be a sustainable gallop without early pressure. Star Banner and potentially The Bureau Club may track in behind the leader, but the majority including Kennington, Chasse Patate, Santiago Boy and Ocean Force will settle towards the rear. With just one natural pace angle, this sets up as a steady-run affair that will develop into a sprint finish. This tactical shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can unleash late kicks over those relying on sustained pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Perola gets an easy lead and kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: The front runner exploits the lack of early pace by dictating terms and proving hard to peg back when getting first run. Hold-up horses find themselves with too much to do against a horse who has conserved energy throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and the field bunches turning for home
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop plays into the hands of horses with natural finishing kicks who can make up ground rapidly. Perola gets swamped by multiple challengers who time their runs to perfection.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Pressure Changes Dynamic
scenarios.trigger: If Star Banner or another tracker decides to pressure Perola from halfway
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates a more honest gallop that suits horses with tactical speed. This scenario reduces the effectiveness of pure hold-up horses while testing the leader's stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Perola sets a crawling pace and the field comes to the boil very late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where positioning and jockey timing become crucial factors. Any horse getting a clear run and showing instant acceleration can capitalize on the chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Perola's fitness after 91-day break and recent wind surgery could see stamina desert late despite tactical advantage
Star Banner's price movement as any strong support would indicate connections expect significant improvement from promising debut
The Bureau Club's early position as habitual slow starter could leave too much ground to make up if pace stays steady
Jockey tactics on Chasse Patate and Kennington as both need cover and clear runs to maximize late finishing kicks
How quickly Perola sets early fractions as overly slow pace would neutralize front-running advantage completely

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: H Key Lails
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning to turf after 86 days off where his record is poor (1-15), but will ensure honest pace
runners_data.spotlight: Races mainly on AW where he has six wins; 1-15 in this sphere and may be worth waiting until he returns to AW.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with turf win already this year, 12 days since last run keeps him sharp
runners_data.spotlight: Has generally been consistent this year, winning for the first time on turf at Musselburgh (7f, good) in April; recorded a rare blip at Leicester last month but back on track when runner-up at Ayr (7f, good to firm) 12 days ago; respected.

runners_data.name: Dandy G Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 168 days off and poor turf record suggests he needs this run back
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice on AW for this yard last year; yet to be placed from five runs on turf and runs off his highest mark; may be better for the run.

runners_data.name: Dutch Kingdom
runners_data.note: Lead/prominent but poor recent form for new yard and cheekpieces return suggests ongoing issues
runners_data.spotlight: All seven wins have been on AW; yet to hit form in two runs for this yard; cheekpieces return but best watched at present.

runners_data.name: Rogue Dynasty
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the expected pace scenario, 73 days off but consistent recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark on her stable debut at Chester (7f, good) last July and has performed with credit on each run since bar a poor effort on soft at Sandown in August; should be better for her reappearance at this track (1m, AW) when fourth of six in March and holds claims in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Portman Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with first-time tongue-tie, lightly raced and only beaten one home on handicap debut here
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly-raced but beat only one home at this track (7f, AW) in April on his handicap debut; a first-time tongue-tie is fitted and still has time on his side.

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who stays this trip well, consistent performer who could benefit if rain arrives
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent sort who got off the mark at Yarmouth (6f, soft) off 2lb lower last September; respectable efforts since and if the rain arrives then that will enhance her claims.

runners_data.name: Amused
runners_data.note: Prominent French import with visor fitted, went close in seller last time and has tactical speed
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French gelding who was unraced at two; made all to land Vichy claimer (very soft) in August and went mighty close for this yard in Leicester seller (good) in October; 25-1 and raced wide before solid fifth of 12 at Kempton (also 7f, AW) in December; showed no improvement in first-time cheekpieces when last of ten on his return at Epsom (8.5f, good) in April and visor returns; best left alone at present.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 236 days off and well held in recent handicaps makes him hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced but well held in handicaps on his last two runs; has been gelded since and returns from a break of 236 days; hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: H Key Lails and Dutch Kingdom will lead from the start, with H Key Lails likely to dominate given his more reliable front-running record. Four horses (Tattie Bogle, Dandy G Boy, Ironist, Amused) all want prominent positions behind the leaders, creating a mid-race squeeze when the field compresses approaching the home turn. The honest early gallop will set up a tactical finish where positioning becomes crucial in the final 2f. This race shape strongly favours HOLD-UP horses like Rogue Dynasty and Portman Blue who can avoid the traffic and finish with one run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet get bunched up turning for home creating traffic problems
scenarios.body: The pace-setters will tire after honest early fractions, leaving gaps for late closers to exploit. Rogue Dynasty and Portman Blue benefit most from clean runs through tired horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner stays honest
scenarios.trigger: If H Key Lails maintains his rhythm and the prominent horses fail to organize
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time in front while the chasers mark each other, allowing him to kick clear when it matters. Dutch Kingdom fades but Amused could emerge from the pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent presser prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses times their move perfectly to avoid the squeeze
scenarios.body: Tattie Bogle or Ironist get first run on the leaders while avoiding traffic behind them. The pace becomes just right for a horse tracking the leaders to strike.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse scenario
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early trying to establish dominance
scenarios.body: The entire field comes back to the hold-up horses who have been conserving energy. Even Big Alex Walmsley becomes competitive despite his poor recent form.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems at the 3f pole when Tattie Bogle, Dandy G Boy, Ironist and Amused all converge behind the leaders
Monitor H Key Lails' jumping early - if he misses the break Dutch Kingdom could steal an uncontested lead
Check if Rogue Dynasty gets the strong pace she needs, as her hold-up style requires others to go hard early
Watch Dutch Kingdom's cheekpieces - if they help him find his old form he could surprise at a price having been written off
Keep an eye on any late market moves for Portman Blue with his first-time tongue-tie and light racing background
